title: Repair
shortDesc: Heating and cooling repairs after a real diagnosis.
fullDesc: {{name}} repairs heating and cooling systems in {{city}} and {{region}}. You hear what failed before anyone sells a new system.
heading: Fix what failed
body: A system that is old is not automatically a system that must be replaced. We separate the failed part from the sales pitch.

faq.a: Most residential brands. Call {{phone}} with the model sticker if you have it.

title: Maintenance
shortDesc: Seasonal checkups so small problems stay small.
fullDesc: {{name}} maintains heating and cooling equipment in {{region}} before peak season.
heading: See the system before it quits
body: Maintenance is a checklist and a conversation about what is wearing out, not a surprise replacement quote.

faq.q: How often should the system be checked?
faq.a: Once before cooling season and once before heating season is the usual plan.

title: Installation
shortDesc: New equipment sized to the house, not a rule of thumb.
fullDesc: {{name}} installs heating and cooling systems in {{city}} after we look at the house, the ducts, and the old equipment.
heading: Size it to the house
body: Oversized equipment short-cycles. We talk through capacity before you pick a model.

faq.q: Do you remove the old equipment?
faq.a: Yes. Haul-away is part of the install scope unless we agree otherwise in writing.

title: Indoor air
shortDesc: Filters, ventilation, and humidity when the house needs them.
fullDesc: {{name}} looks at filtration and ventilation in {{region}} homes as part of the comfort system, not a separate mystery.
heading: Air is part of the system
body: We recommend a change when the house needs it, and we skip the catalog when it does not.

faq.q: Will a new filter fix a weak system?
faq.a: A clogged filter can. A failed compressor will not. We test before we sell.
